name: Adnan Menderes International Airport
before:
Izmir's airport, 14 km south west of the city in the Gaziemir district, and the natural arrival for most of Izmir province. It served 12.7 million passengers in 2025, fifth busiest in Turkey.

It is heavily domestic. Of those 12.7 million, 7.6 million were domestic passengers, and it ranks fourth in Turkey on domestic traffic alone.

There is a structural quirk worth knowing. The airport has two runways but they cannot be used at the same time, because they sit too close together and the second one long lacked a dedicated taxiway. In practice 16L/34R is the working runway and 16R/34L serves mostly as a parallel taxiway, kept as a backup for maintenance. So the airport runs on one runway.

The international terminal opened in September 2006 and the domestic terminal in March 2014. A new apron completed in March 2020 lifted remote parking from 35 stands to 61.

It is named after Adnan Menderes, the former Turkish prime minister.
after:
Izmir's airport, 14 km from the city centre in the Gaziemir district. It served 12.7 million passengers in 2025, fifth busiest in Turkey.

Most of its traffic is domestic. Of those 12.7 million, 7.6 million were domestic passengers, and it ranks fourth in Turkey on domestic traffic alone.

The international terminal opened in 2006, and a new domestic terminal followed.

It is named after Adnan Menderes, the former Turkish prime minister.

claims.note: Eurostat's 2025 table of passengers carried covers all 872 airports that report to it, 58 of them Turkish. An airport's total (schedule and coverage both TOTAL) sits at value index airport x 28. Izmir is airport 832, value 23296: 12,665,508. Above it: Istanbul (870, value 24360: 84,512,620), Sabiha Gokcen (868, value 24304: 48,407,144), Antalya (816, value 22848: 39,000,664) and Ankara Esenboga (814, value 22792: 13,926,576). Next below is Dalaman (836, value 23408: 5,578,270). Wikipedia gives the same order.

claims.claim: two runways that cannot be used together; 16L/34R the working runway, 16R/34L a taxiway and backup; so one runway in practice
claims.wasBefore: The airport has two runways but they cannot be used at the same time, because they sit too close together and the second one long lacked a dedicated taxiway. In practice 16L/34R is the working runway and 16R/34L serves mostly as a parallel taxiway, kept as a backup for maintenance. So the airport runs on one runway.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The airport and TAV confirm two runways but say nothing on how they are used; SkyVector had no page for the airport (404); DHMI, which owns the airport and publishes its aeronautical data, refused (502, one try). Wikipedia itself says a parallel taxiway has since been built, so the arrangement may have changed. 'Two runways' is not kept on its own: without the caveat it would suggest more capacity than the old text meant.

claims.claim: the international terminal opened in September
claims.wasBefore: The international terminal opened in September 2006
claims.why: The month rests on Wikipedia alone; TAV and the airport give 2006. Softened (above).

claims.claim: the domestic terminal opened in March 2014
claims.wasBefore: and the domestic terminal in March 2014
claims.why: Good sources disagree on the date. Wikipedia says the new domestic terminal opened around March 2014; TAV says it began operating the domestic terminal in 2012 after a 416 million euro investment; the airport's award list shows the new building still under construction in 2013, which sits better with 2014, but no second source gives 2014. Softened to 'a new domestic terminal followed' (above) rather than pick one.
